key_insight: Energy-Based Generative Replay (EB-Gen) reduces forgetting by using a Hopfield network’s intrinsic dynamics to generate replay samples for continual learning.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support edge-friendly continual learning without external data buffers or a separate generator, though no solid-mechanics application is evaluated.
method: Train a Hopfield network using Equilibrium Propagation.
Generate pseudo-data representing prior tasks by relaxing a frozen network copy.
Rehearse on generated samples while learning new classes.
evidence_signal: On class-incremental Split MNIST and Split CIFAR10, EB-Gen achieves reported average accuracies of 75% and 64%, respectively, with comparisons against FineTune, ER, Gen-Replay, SRC and joint training.
watch_item: Maintaining a frozen network copy and relaxing it to generate samples incur memory and computation costs; edge-hardware efficiency is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks
